en: Itivuttaka 48 Dukanipāta, Second Chapter Thus it was said by the Blessed One; having been said by the Sublime One, it was so stated by the Teacher: “Monks, there are these two kinds of persons found existing in the world. What two? The person who is a doer of evil deeds and the person who is a doer of good deeds. These, monks, are the two kinds of persons found existing in the world. Thus it was said by the Blessed One; having been said by the Sublime One, it was so stated by the Teacher. And in reference to this, it was said: “The one who does evil deeds, And the one who does good deeds— These two, indeed, are seen in the world, As those who fare according to their own karma. Thus it was said by the Blessed One; having been said by the Sublime One, it was so stated by the Teacher. And this is how it was stated by the Teacher. Thus have I heard. The Discourse on Those Bound for the States of Misery.
Thus it was said by the Blessed One, so I have heard:
"Monks, these two are bound for the states of misery, destined for hell, if they do not abandon this."
Which two?

One who is not a practitioner of the holy life but claims to be a practitioner of the holy life, and one who groundlessly accuses another who is practicing the holy life, perfect and pure, of unchastity.
These, monks, are the two who are destined for states of deprivation, destined for hell, and from whom this [state] cannot be escaped.”
The Blessed One spoke this matter.
Regarding this, it is said:
"One who speaks what is untrue goes to hell."
Or he who, having done [an evil deed], says, "I did not do it"—
both of these, upon passing away,
become equal in the next world, being men of base actions.
Many with saffron robes around their necks,
evil-natured and unrestrained,
are wicked because of their wicked deeds.
They are reborn in hell.
Better it would be to swallow a glowing iron ball,
hot as a crest of flame, than that.
"And whatever an immoral person, unrestrained, might eat as alms from the kingdom"—
this matter too was spoken by the Blessed One; thus have I heard.
The eleventh.
